checklist.name: left ventricular hypertrophy
quotes: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) is the most common cardiac manifestation at presentation for both sexes
children and adolescents can have accelerated hypertrophy of the cardiomyocytes, resulting in severe LVH
checklist.why: The commonest and defining cardiac presentation in both sexes; severity in the young distinguishes Danon disease.

checklist.name: dilated or hypokinetic left ventricle (reduced ejection fraction)
quotes: 30% to 50% of female individuals can present with a dilated or hypokinetic nondilated phenotype
the hypertrophic heart becomes hypokinetic, followed by wall thinning and possible dilation
checklist.why: The review's sex-distinguishing cardiac phenotype (frequent in females) and the late stage of the hypertrophic course.

checklist.name: heart failure
quotes: Most patients with Danon disease will experience symptomatic heart failure.
checklist.why: The review names symptomatic heart failure as the usual course in both sexes.

checklist.name: right ventricular hypertrophy
quotes: female individuals presented with asymmetric LVH, right ventricular hypertrophy, and both hypertrophic and dilated phenotypes
Concomitant RVH
checklist.why: Listed as a red flag and reported more in females, so it helps separate sex patterns.

checklist.name: left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
quotes: left ventricular outflow tract obstruction can be present in one quarter of patients with Danon disease
checklist.why: Present in about a quarter of patients per the review and routinely stated in echocardiography reports.

checklist.name: late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac MRI
quotes: In Danon disease, late gadolinium enhancement is frequently present with extensive patchy and diffuse patterns.
Extensive LGE with sparing of the midseptum
checklist.why: Frequent imaging finding and a red flag; case reports with CMR state it as present or absent.

checklist.name: ventricular pre-excitation (short PR, delta wave or Wolff-Parkinson-White)
quotes: Early manifestations include short PR and/or delta waves
Pre-excitation secondary to Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome or fasciculoventricular pathways, which may be an early marker of disease, is common in both male (69%) and female individuals (27%)
checklist.why: A hallmark ECG finding with sex-specific frequencies, more frequent than in other hypertrophic heart disease.

checklist.name: atrioventricular block
quotes: High-degree heart block or sinus node dysfunction requiring pacemaker implantation is also highly prevalent
the high incidence of atrial fibrillation and advanced atrioventricular bloc
checklist.why: Highly prevalent conduction disease and a red flag (AV block) in the review.

checklist.name: supraventricular tachycardia (atrial fibrillation or flutter)
quotes: Supraventricular tachycardias, including atrial flutter and atrial fibrillation, as well as ventricular arrhythmias, are common
checklist.why: Common arrhythmias in the review (about 60% with ventricular arrhythmias combined).

checklist.name: ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation
quotes: intraventricular conduction disturbances and malignant ventricular arrhythmia are common
nonsustained ventricular tachycardia is not rare in Danon disease
checklist.why: Malignant ventricular arrhythmia is common and drives risk; case reports state it explicitly.

checklist.name: proximal muscle weakness (skeletal myopathy)
quotes: weakness reported predominantly in proximal muscles, including pelvic girdle and axial muscles
Neuromuscular involvement is frequent in male individuals and presents as progressive proximal muscle weakness.
checklist.why: Part of the classic triad; more frequent in males.

checklist.name: elevated creatine kinase
quotes: Creatine kinase and transaminase levels are typically elevated in male individuals
Elevated serum CK
checklist.why: Typical laboratory finding in males and a red flag; can precede the cardiomyopathy diagnosis.

checklist.name: intellectual disability, cognitive impairment or learning difficulties
quotes: Mild cognitive impairment and learning difficulties have been reported in at least 80% of affected male individuals and between 6% and 47% of female patients.
checklist.why: Part of the classic triad, with clearly different frequencies by sex.

checklist.name: developmental delay (including delayed motor milestones)
quotes: Developmental delay
delayed motor milestones can affect 1 in 5 male individuals
checklist.why: A red flag in the review and part of diagnostic criterion C; usually reported in children.

checklist.name: attention deficit disorder or ADHD
quotes: Young individuals with the disease often carry the diagnosis of attention deficit disorder before receiving a definitive diagnosis of Danon disease.
attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
checklist.why: Often diagnosed before Danon disease and part of diagnostic criterion C.

checklist.name: mood or anxiety disorder
quotes: Psychiatric disorders can be subtle and range from behavioral abnormalities to mood and anxiety disorders
checklist.why: Psychiatric involvement reported in up to 69% in one case series cited by the review.

checklist.name: pigmentary retinopathy or retinal dystrophy
quotes: Vision impairment, mainly pigmentary retinopathy and myopia, have been classically described in patients with Danon disease
loss of retinal pigment in the retinal epithelium and cone-rod dystrophy
checklist.why: The review's characteristic eye finding and a red flag.

checklist.name: myopia
quotes: Vision abnormalities, such as retinopathy and myopia, occur equally in both sexes.
checklist.why: Named alongside retinopathy as a classic visual feature of the disease.

checklist.name: elevated liver enzymes (transaminases)
quotes: Creatine kinase and transaminase levels are typically elevated in male individuals
elevated transaminases without hepatic synthetic dysfunction
checklist.why: Common laboratory finding that can precede the cardiac diagnosis.

checklist.name: hepatomegaly
quotes: Hepatomegaly has been reported
checklist.why: The review's named gastrointestinal/hepatic sign.

left_out: elevated troponin or natriuretic peptides (BNP/NT-proBNP): monitoring biomarkers of cardiac injury and wall stress; heart failure item covers the clinical state
sinus node dysfunction: named with heart block but cut to stay at 20; less often reported separately
high ECG voltage and repolarization abnormalities: would overlap with left ventricular hypertrophy as recorded from ECG
intraventricular conduction disturbances: named once; cut to stay at 20
embolic stroke or intracardiac thrombus: described as something that 'can also occur', a less typical complication
cardiac arrest and sudden arrhythmic death: outcomes, excluded by rule 3
heart transplantation and end-stage heart failure: outcomes or treatments
myalgias and decreased exercise capacity: called nonspecific by the review; exercise capacity can be cardiac or muscular
congestive hepatopathy: a sequela of advanced heart failure rather than a primary feature
elevated LDH: listed only among lab tests; low yield in case reports
behavioral abnormalities (other than ADHD): too vague to code consistently
apical sparing strain pattern and increased T1/ECV: specialist imaging rarely reported in case reports
pulmonary manifestations: named in the review but not described specifically
autophagic vacuoles on biopsy and absent LAMP-2 protein expression: diagnostic findings that define the disease
syncope or presyncope: mentioned only in the context of ICD decisions, not as a disease feature
notes: Built only from PMID 37821174 (JACC State-of-the-Art Review, 2023). Ten of 20 items are cardiac, matching the review's emphasis. 'Dilated or hypokinetic left ventricle' is a structural/functional finding and 'heart failure' the clinical syndrome; extractors should not infer one from the other. 'Elevated creatine kinase' and 'elevated liver enzymes' are laboratory items kept separate from 'proximal muscle weakness'; the review notes transaminase rises may reflect muscle injury rather than liver injury, so record what the paper states. 'Intellectual disability' and 'developmental delay' are kept as siblings; a paper saying only 'developmental delay' should not be recorded as intellectual disability. The quote 'advanced atrioventricular bloc' preserves the review's typo.
